revenue.why: Knos runs on Solana devnet only: every fee taken is test money. Nothing has been sold.

treasury.what: the fee owner: Knos's Squads vault (a program-derived address of the Squads program). Every fee the program takes lands in a token account it owns.
treasury.moves_by: a Squads proposal of the vault; nothing in Knos signs for it

verification.what: one verification (an evaluation of a pull request or a result) on runners Knos hosts
verification.note: Checking stays free for public repositories and on your own runners; this is the Meter line of the price book.

payout.what: the fee on every release from escrow to a payee (the Acceptance line): the funder pays it on top of the amount
payout.payer: funder, on top of the amount

bounty.what: a bounty is a knos_pay work order: the same fee, taken by the program and sent to the treasury at payout (the on-chain part of the bounty fee, bounty_platform)
bounty.refund: a bounty refunded after its deadline returns the amount and the fee

bounty_platform.what: the Knos bounty fee: 5% of the bounty, paid by the funder; the on-chain bounty fee (0.30%, at least 0.05) is part of it, not added to it
bounty_platform.collected: the program takes the on-chain bounty fee at payout; the rest (5% minus that fee) is invoiced off chain, because knos_pay's fee is compiled into the program (0.30%) and charging 5% on chain needs a program upgrade through the Squads vault
bounty_platform.rationale: 5% of the bounty: a starting price, to revisit once the cost per verification is measured
bounty_platform.source: founder decision 14 Oct 2026 (DECISIONS.md item 2). The comparison with Algora's fee to organisations is the founder's; Algora's pricing page (algora.io/pricing) answered 404 on 14 Oct 2026, so no Algora figure is stated here

lab_order.what: the Knos fee on a lab order paid through a Knos escrow (the lab is paid when its protocol and QC verdict passes): 3% of the order; the on-chain payout fee (0.30%, at least 0.05) is part of it, not added to it
lab_order.collected: the program takes the payout fee at release; the rest (3% minus that fee) is invoiced off chain until a program upgrade carries it. Who bears it (the buyer on top, or deducted from the lab's payment) is not set by the decision
lab_order.rationale: labs already pay 2% to 3% of an invoice just to be paid sooner; Knos's 3% buys payment from escrow on a verdict
lab_order.source: founder decision 14 Oct 2026 (DECISIONS.md item 2). Scientist.com SciPay: suppliers pay 3.00% (NET30), 2.50% (NET45), 2.00% (NET60), https://www.scientist.com/scipay/ (read 14 Oct 2026)

funding.what: opening an escrow (a graduation milestone or a pre-order): the program holds the payout fee with the money and takes it only at release

graduation.what: a fee on the value of the milestone escrow and the pre-order pool released after a claim graduates, above the payout fee
graduation.collected: by contract, off chain, until a knos_pay build carries it (a program upgrade); on chain today only the payout fee is taken
graduation.rationale: 0.5% of money raised: a starting price, to revisit once the cost per verification is measured

task_package.what: Knos's share of a sale of a sealed task package (issue + hidden tests + cheat rules); the maintainer keeps the rest
task_package.market: labs pay 200 to 2,000 USD per task (Epoch AI, 12 Jan 2026); robustness to reward hacking is the top buying criterion (same source)
task_package.collected: off chain, by contract (a sale of a task package is not a knos_pay order today)
task_package.rationale: the maintainer who wrote the task keeps 90%; Knos keeps 10%

x402_check.what: a paid check bought by an agent over x402 (knos-order scheme), in devnet USDC (test money), sold in packs because the smallest order is 5.00
x402_check.mint: devnet USDC (test money) until the cost per verification is measured
x402_check.rationale: a per-check price for agents paying over x402, apart from the hosted Meter line of the price book (0.002 after the free month)

splits.what: the fixed share of every payout each contributor role receives, in basis points; one order pays at most 4 payees, so 4 roles
splits.rounding: each share is rounded down; the last payee receives what is left, exactly as knos_pay pays (order_pay.rs)

cloud.what: Knos Cloud: paid credits for hosted verification (runners, sealed-test storage, receipts, Gate for private repositories). Everything stays open source (MIT) and self-hosting stays free.
cloud.rationale: three monthly tiers of 20, 100 and 200 USD, each with 10% bonus credit (22, 110 and 220 USD of credit a month)
cloud.source: founder decision 14 Oct 2026 (DECISIONS.md item 2), on the Nous Portal pattern (see shape_from); the 10% bonus is the founder's, not a sourced Nous figure
cloud.units_what: what one credit is worth and what each use consumes are not decided: credit_usd, consumes and so each tier's credit count are placeholders
cloud.enterprise: by contract (the Control line of the price book)
cloud.shape_from: Nous Research's Portal sells $20/$100/$200 monthly tiers (TechCrunch, 7 Oct 2026, citing the WSJ; unaudited). Knos's tier prices match it by founder decision (14 Oct 2026); the credit unit is a placeholder.

nous.said: Nous Research: open core (MIT) plus hosted subscriptions with credits (Portal $20/$100/$200 tiers) plus enterprise; about $36M annualized revenue by mid-September 2026; raised $90M at a $1.5B valuation
nous.source: TechCrunch, 7 Oct 2026, citing the Wall Street Journal

epoch_tasks.said: labs pay 200 to 2,000 USD per verified task; robustness to reward hacking is the top buying criterion

scipay.said: Scientist.com SciPay: suppliers pay 3.00% (NET30), 2.50% (NET45) or 2.00% (NET60) to be paid early, plus 0.75% for currencies other than USD

graduation_demo.what: the MONEY graduation demo on Solana devnet: real transactions on the public knos_pay program, SYNTHETIC claims and verdicts, a test mint of the demo's own; test money, 0 revenue

model.label: MODEL: revenue for the volumes typed in, at the fee config's rates. Not a forecast; no volume here is measured. The payout line is a lower bound: the floor is charged per release, and the model knows only the month's total and count.

one_billion.label: DERIVED: 1,000,000,000 USD divided by each rate in config/fees.yaml. Arithmetic on the rates, not a forecast, not a plan.
